reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — User input flows through param → bar → sql, and on the successful query path (line 58-61), sql is printed directly to response.getWriter() WITHOUT HTML encoding. Encoding only occurs in the EmptyResultDataAccessException catch block (line 63-64). Since the primary success path lacks encoding, XSS is possible. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-TP — User input flows through param → bar → sql, concatenated directly into SQL query string without sanitization, enabling SQL injection. Both alerts represent real vulnerabilities on their respective paths.

evidence.note: User input extracted from request parameters flows through Test.doSomething to bar, then concatenated into SQL string at line 58
SQL injection vulnerability: bar (containing user input) concatenated directly into SQL without sanitization
XSS alert refers to this location, but encoding only applies to error path; success path prints sql unencoded
